Hi Samir — thanks for the clear ask. Confirming Redwood's approach for the referenced report (Redwood SOC 2 Type II covering 2026-04-01 through 2026-06-30):

- Cutoff semantics: The report period is inclusive of the calendar date June 30, 2026. All system-generated timestamps and evidence we provide are normalized to UTC for audit purposes. That means an event stamped 2026-06-30T23:59:59Z is in-scope.

- Snapshot practice: For point-in-time evidence we provide manifested snapshots taken at 00:00:00 UTC following the stated cutoff (i.e., a snapshot taken 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z representing state at the end of 2026-06-30). We also retain rolling logs in our cold storage for 90 days post-period for audit retrieval.

- Bridge letters / rollforward: We can provide a signed bridge letter when customers require explicit continuity for events immediately after the cutoff (commonly used for short rollforwards). Our standard bridge-letter language confirms that the controls remained in place and operated consistently from the report cutoff through a specified short window (we typically limit to 7 days for operational statements).

- Artifacts we can attach: PDF of the finalized SOC 2 report, a CSV manifest of the log snapshot(s) with object IDs and generation timestamps, and a draft bridge-letter (Word).

I'm attaching the SOC 2 PDF and a draft bridge-letter for your review. Neha — can you confirm the manifest file and whether the 90-day cold storage policy shows the snapshot object IDs for June 30? Samir / KPMG: happy to adjust the bridge-letter wording if your auditor prefers different phrasing.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head, Compliance & Privacy
Redwood Inference
